fixture.result: Socket construction is patched to raise, so any network attempt fails. Importer output retained participants/date/url/exchanges but dropped source context. Direct write_transcript preserved context. A two-exchange transcript captured constructor date/url/participants and previous-answer arguments ('', then 'out1'); fresh generation stopped at missing #2 despite #3 existing. After adding #2, rerun processed filename order 1,2,3 even with intentionally out-of-order dates 1840, 1841, 1839; this demonstrates enumeration order, not chronological enforcement. Missing date/url keys raise KeyError in process_transcripts. Corpus duplicate suppression blocked a repeated link within one append and on a second pass. This does not prove Chroma duplication is impossible across stale collections or changed IDs.

corrected_or_qualified: The importer does not preserve context even for an input already in transcript schema; it calls write_transcript without context.
The strict < filter is only active when Chroma metadata proves the collection is dated; an old undated collection skips the filter.
Null/unparseable corpus dates become date_num 0 and remain retrievable, so null cannot safely represent unknown historical availability.
One transcript-level date applies to every exchange in that file; there is no per-exchange date or section chronology.
Corpus retrieval returns participants/url/title metadata but the summarizer prompt frames retrieved prose as the persona author's memory; no verified incoming-only attribution channel exists.
Query-before-store avoids the current exchange only in a clean run; it does not exclude a copy already in corpus/Chroma, prior persistent runs, or overlapping sections.
Corpus duplicate suppression is link-based and works in the fixture; it is not a complete target/section/semantic duplicate policy.
HF loss masking is delegated to opbdh/TRL via completion_only_loss=True; no local training or collator execution was performed, so masking is format-ready but training-unverified.
